chapters.summary: Cecilia Ellis of NYPIRG testifies in support of Resolution 362, noting the bottle bill is the state's most successful recycling program, urging expansion of covered containers, and citing cost savings of $34.9-$80 million for NYC if the law is modernized. chapters.title: Cecilia Ellis (NYPIRG) testifies in support of Resolution 362 and bottle bill modernization

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cecilia Ellis
utterances.text: Hi, thanks.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cecilia Ellis
utterances.text: Okay, so my name is Cecilia Ellis.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cecilia Ellis
utterances.text: I am Policy and Communications Manager for the New York Public Interest Research Group, NYPERG.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cecilia Ellis
utterances.text: Consumer protection, environmental preservation, public health, higher education, energy and climate, and government reforms are our principal areas of concern.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cecilia Ellis
utterances.text: We're testifying today in support of Resolution 362.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cecilia Ellis
utterances.text: My testimony summarizes the written version I've submitted, written by Blair Horner, our senior policy advisor.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cecilia Ellis
utterances.text: As you know and have heard, the bottle bill has been on the books for over four decades and is the law that requires a nickel deposit on beverage containers and water bottles and cans.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cecilia Ellis
utterances.text: Was originally designed as an anti-litter measure, but has become the most successful recycling program in general for the entire state.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cecilia Ellis
utterances.text: Two-thirds of covered beverage containers are redeemed, and we need to expand the definition of which beverage containers are covered by the law.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cecilia Ellis
utterances.text: Many containers that did not exist in 1982 are ubiquitous today and need to be covered, so we should be expanding that bottle bill.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cecilia Ellis
utterances.text: Included in the written testimony are some examples of bottles like this vitamin water that is redeemable, but the Gatorade sports drink is not redeemable because it didn't exist.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cecilia Ellis
utterances.text: We have a lot of drinks, a lot of examples of that in our written testimony.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cecilia Ellis
utterances.text: We also have a recent report analyzing the cost savings to municipalities if New York does modernize the law.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cecilia Ellis
utterances.text: As you heard,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cecilia Ellis
utterances.text: heard from Ryan, New York City taxpayers could see a reduction in solid waste disposal and litter cleanup costs, totaling anywhere from $34.9 million to as much as $80 million.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cecilia Ellis
utterances.text: Of course, the city budgets far exceed the savings estimated in the report, but as you know,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cecilia Ellis
utterances.text: Budget's tightening.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cecilia Ellis
utterances.text: We've heard all day today costs are going up.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cecilia Ellis
utterances.text: Landfills are reaching capacity.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cecilia Ellis
utterances.text: Any steps to curb solid waste and solid waste costs need to be embraced.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cecilia Ellis
utterances.text: It's time for a dime.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cecilia Ellis
utterances.text: So therefore, NYPR urges the council to support this resolution at the...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cecilia Ellis
utterances.text: States to expand the state's bottle bill.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Caitlin Vietoro
utterances.text: My name is Caitlin Vietoro, and I'm the New York City Policy Fellow at the New York League of Conservation Voters.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Caitlin Vietoro
utterances.text: Thank you, Chair Sanchez and members of the Committee on Sanitation, for the opportunity to comment.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Caitlin Vietoro
utterances.text: NYLCV strongly supports our city's zero waste by 2030 goal to curb our greenhouse gas emissions and send less waste to landfills located in low-income and communities of color.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Caitlin Vietoro
utterances.text: The pollution from landfills and incinerators in these communities disproportionately cause health issues and compound existing environmental and racial inequities.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Caitlin Vietoro
utterances.text: Our city needs to move towards a system where waste is reduced first before the burden of it can impact environmental justice communities.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Caitlin Vietoro
utterances.text: Our written testimony outlines several priorities, including reducing our reliance on plastic products, particularly single-use ones.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Caitlin Vietoro
utterances.text: We encourage the city to reduce procurement of single-use plastic products.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Caitlin Vietoro
utterances.text: If compostable products are utilized, we must also ensure that composting facilities can accept them.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Caitlin Vietoro
utterances.text: We strongly support organic waste recycling.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Caitlin Vietoro
utterances.text: We supported the council passing L.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Caitlin Vietoro
utterances.text: 85 of 2023, establishing a city-wide residential organics program, and we're pleased at the expansion of categories of establishments subject to commercial organic waste recycling.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Caitlin Vietoro
utterances.text: We hope DSNY continues to prioritize curbside organic enforcement with education.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Caitlin Vietoro
utterances.text: DSNY should continue in investing composting infrastructure and continue working with the community composting network to build awareness and inspire organic waste recycling.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Caitlin Vietoro
utterances.text: Increasing awareness and accessibility of textile recycling is imperative.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Caitlin Vietoro
utterances.text: We support the direction of Intro 256 sponsored by Councilmember Hudson, and we recommend the bill develop a timeframe requiring DSNY to mandate textile collection for all city households, institutions, and NYCHA.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Caitlin Vietoro
utterances.text: The bill should consider capital funding needs, its recycling capacity to accept textiles, and more.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Caitlin Vietoro
utterances.text: NYLCB strongly supports DSNY's work advancing an extended producer responsibility for packaging program at the state level.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Caitlin Vietoro
utterances.text: We encourage the state and DSNY to explore the potential for other EPR programs for difficult to recycle materials such as mattresses.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Caitlin Vietoro
utterances.text: And we look forward to working with the City Council and Mamdani administration to ensure we meet our zero waste by 2030 goals.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Caitlin Vietoro
utterances.text: Thank you for the opportunity.

utterances.speaker: Justin E. Sanchez
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Caitlin Vietoro
utterances.text: Thank you.

summary: Oversight hearing of the Committee on Sanitation and Solid Waste Management on waste valorization and the circular economy, covering textile recycling, nightlife district street cleaning, community composting on parkland, and bottle bill expansion.

DSNY Commissioner Gregory Anderson and DEP officials testified on recycling programs, composting infrastructure, anaerobic digestion at Newtown Creek and Hunts Point, textile collection challenges, and the draft Solid Waste Management Plan.

Public testimony included advocates from NRDC, NYPIRG, Sure We Can, NYC Environmental Justice Alliance, and others urging support for the bottle bill, textile recycling mandates, and community composting expansion.
